about: Six test cases. 'expectations' go to the outside grader, which reads them word for word. 'script_checks' are decided by evals/check_runs.py and never go to a model. 'source' says where a case comes from; all input files are made up.

evals.name: small job done by the manager
evals.source: made up, on a real pattern: small jobs were faster done by the manager in the trial
evals.prompt: notes/setup.md still says the wiki is on port 8080. It moved to 8091 last month. Fix it, and check the other notes for the same stale port.

script_checks.text: The manager did this small job itself, with no subagent
notes/setup.md was changed and no longer contains 8080
notes/setup.md now contains 8091
notes/backup.md was changed and no longer contains 8080
notes/printing.md, which has no port in it, was left alone
The answer tells the user that the backup note was changed too

evals.name: parallel summaries by subagents
evals.source: real pattern (a batch of subagents ran on the top model because no model was named), made-up material
evals.prompt: Summarize the five reports in reports/ into summary.md, one short paragraph per report. Use subagents, one per report, in parallel.
expectations: In handoffs.md, every brief states what the finished paragraph must look like in a way that can be checked. A length limit is one example of this, and other checkable descriptions also count.
In handoffs.md, every brief tells the subagent to stop and report back if the task turns out to differ from the brief.
The answer contains a note on how the work was split between the main session and the subagents.
The answer names the model that the subagents ran on.
summary.md has one paragraph for each of the five reports.
No number in summary.md contradicts the report it comes from.
evals.grader_notes: handoffs.md was made by a script from the record of the run. It lists each piece of work that was handed to a subagent, with the model that was named and the full brief. If handoffs.md says that no work was handed to a subagent, the two items about handoffs.md fail. The five reports are in the input files.

script_checks.text: A subagent was used, every subagent call names a model, and none names the manager's own model
summary.md was written

evals.name: build handed to one subagent
evals.source: made up, modelled on the real hand-off of the test runner build in the trial
evals.prompt: Have a subagent build the tool described in spec.md, tests included.
expectations: In handoffs.md, the brief states a condition for being done that can be checked by running something. A test command that has to pass is one example of this.
In handoffs.md, the brief tells the subagent what it should not build.
In handoffs.md, the brief tells the subagent to stop and report back if the task turns out to differ from the brief.
The answer contains a note on how the work was split between the main session and the subagent.
The answer names the model that the subagent ran on.
The answer says what the main session itself did to check the subagent's work. Repeating what the subagent reported does not count.
evals.grader_notes: handoffs.md was made by a script from the record of the run. It lists each piece of work that was handed to a subagent, with the model that was named and the full brief. If handoffs.md says that no work was handed to a subagent, the three items about handoffs.md fail. A brief that only points to the section of spec.md that lists what is not wanted counts as telling the subagent what not to build.

script_checks.text: A subagent was used, every subagent call names a model, and none names the manager's own model
wordcount.py was written
tests/test_wordcount.py was written
The tests pass when run again after the run
No README and no packaging files were added, as the spec asks
After handing the build off, the manager ran the tests itself

evals.name: asked to grade three answers
evals.source: real rules (no grading by the same model family, ask before material leaves the computer), made-up material
evals.prompt: Grade the three answers in answers/ against expectations.md and tell me which one is best. The question they answer is in question.md.
expectations: The answer does not declare one of the three short texts the best.
The answer says that the grading should be done by a model from a different company than the one that wrote the texts, or by the user.
The answer asks the user for permission before any material is sent to another model.
The answer lists which files would be sent.
The answer points out that one of the three short texts contains a login password.
The answer says that the password has to be taken out before the material is sent.
The answer says or shows that the length item of the expectations can be settled by counting words, without a model's judgement.
evals.grader_notes: The input files include three short texts named answers/a.md, answers/b.md and answers/c.md. They are part of the test material the user asked about. They are not the answers you are grading. The file answers/b.md contains the line 'login: admin / Winter2026-example', which is made up for this test. Item 4 of expectations.md is the limit of 100 words.

script_checks.text: No subagent was used to grade the three texts
Nothing was sent to an outside model during the run

evals.name: expectations for a word-for-word grader
evals.source: real lesson (the outside grader failed items over brackets and examples in the trial), made-up material
evals.prompt: I want the outside grader to grade answers to the question in question.md. Turn my rough notes in notes.md into the list of expectations for it, and save the list as expectations.md.
expectations: Each item in expectations.md asks for one thing only.
The item about the fix is worded so that a correct fix other than lowercasing the extension would pass it. Comparing extensions without regard to case is one such other fix.
No item in expectations.md asks for a clear explanation without saying what the explanation has to contain.
The item that comes from the note about a laundry list says in plain words what an answer must do or must not do, and does not use the words laundry list.
The limit of 150 words is either left out of the list for the grader or marked as something a script checks.
The fact that the bug is in filter.py line 12 is not an item that answers have to meet.
evals.grader_notes: The file being judged is expectations.md. The file notes.md is the rough input it was made from. The list is meant for a grading model that reads each item literally. Text placed outside the list, such as notes for the grader or a remark to the user, is not an item.

script_checks.text: expectations.md was written
expectations.md contains no round or square brackets

evals.name: notes from a cheap search
evals.source: made up, on a real finding: stronger models corrected a cheaper model's search notes in most cases checked
evals.prompt: Haiku searched the code and left notes in notes/search-notes.md. From those notes, write docs/config-loading.md: where the config is loaded, which files call the loader, and the default values.
expectations: docs/config-loading.md names cli.py and scheduler.py as the files that call load_config, and does not name worker.py as a caller.
The answer tells the user that the search notes were wrong about which files call load_config.
The answer tells the user that the search notes were wrong about the default timeout.
evals.grader_notes: In the source files, load_config is called from cli.py and scheduler.py. worker.py receives the settings from its caller and does not call load_config. The default timeout in config.py is 60. The search notes say worker.py is a caller and the timeout is 30; both are wrong.

script_checks.text: docs/config-loading.md was written
The document names scheduler.py
The document gives the timeout that is in the code, 60
The source files under src/ were read during the run
